summary: High-rate 5xx elevation during customer concurrency ramp; HTTP/2 stream stall + runtime worker crash-loop
description:
Issue summary:
Customers started seeing spike in 5xx (primarily 502/503) on a streaming chat route for LexiSearch's tenant during a planned concurrency ramp. Errors began at ~2026-03-12T14:05 PDT and persisted as a sustained elevated error rate for ~30 minutes before partial mitigation.

Impact:
- LexiSearch reported increased failed streaming sessions and timeouts for interactive chat flows (~40% failure rate at peak).
- Errors observed at API gateway layer (502, 503) with rapid upstream restarts reported by runtime autoscale groups.
- A single tenant (dedicated pool) appears to have driven the pattern during a traffic ramp.

Why this ticket is different:
Multiple prior tickets focus on accept-queue or kvcache thrash. This incident shows an HTTP/2 per-connection stream stall pattern combined with runtime worker crash-loops tied to an internal model-variant swap path that amplifies memory use under rapid stream resumption. That combination created a cascade not seen in recent reproductions.
steps_to_reproduce: Start a large number (200+) of simultaneous streaming sessions for a single tenant to the /v1/chat/stream endpoint using HTTP/2 multiplexing from a single client IP.
Use long-lived streaming sessions that keep an idle heartbeat open but send intermittent prompt updates (mix of short and long prompts).
Observe gateway metrics and runtime pod logs as concurrency ramps over 5 minutes.
logs:
Excerpt from api-gateway at 2026-03-12T14:07:21 PDT: 'upstream response returned non-2xx: 503 Service Unavailable'
Runtime log snippet from runtime-abc-3: '[2026-03-12T14:07:19Z] worker(3) OOM: process killed by OOM-killer while performing variant quant swap; backtrace...
[2026-03-12T14:07:22Z] watchdog: worker restarted (exit code 137)'
Proxy trace: repeated HTTP/2 RST_STREAM for stream ids 15..110 with GOAWAYs observed when the runtime pod restarted.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Observed correlation between burst start time and elevated 5xx at API gateway. Traced failing requests to a small set of runtime pods in the customer's dedicated pool.

SRE findings: Runtime worker processes showed memory growth spikes immediately prior to exits (exit code 137). Core dumps indicate allocation spike during model variant fallback path (quantized->fp16 fallback under memory pressure).

Hypothesis A: HTTP/2 stream head-of-line stalls cause request timeouts and backpressure in the gateway; combined with hedged retries, this created concentrated load on a subset of runtime workers leading to their memory pressure and OOMs.

Hypothesis B: A model-variant swap routine (on-demand quant->full precision reload) is triggered on cache miss when multiple concurrent streams hit cold KV cache; the swap temporarily doubles memory footprint causing OOM under high concurrency.
Telemetry: CPU of affected runtimes modest (~30-50%) while RSS memory shot from 22GB to ~46GB during swap window; NVMe IO spiked, and kernel dmesg shows io_wait increases.
temporary_workarounds: Applied tenant-level concurrency cap: reduced max concurrent streaming sessions from 600 -> 150 for LexiSearch which immediately reduced peak OOM events.
Enabled gateway per-connection stream limit (max concurrent streams=50) to reduce head-of-line blocking from single client IPs.
Pinned customer's route to an older model-variant that does not perform on-demand quant->fp16 swaps while engineering investigates.
Advised customer to stagger session ramp (30s window) instead of an instantaneous ramp as mitigation until fix is deployed.
resolution_notes: Work in progress. Short-term mitigations (concurrency cap + route pinning + gateway stream limit) reduced error rate from ~40% to ~3% for LexiSearch. Engineering to deliver a safer variant-swap flow and add guardrails in runtime to avoid doubling memory footprint during concurrent swaps. Plan: 1) add a serialized quant-swap lock per model shard to prevent simultaneous swaps, 2) pre-warm variant cache during tenant warmup, 3) add runtime circuit that rejects new swaps under memory pressure. ETA for patch: 2026-03-18. Rollout: canary -> regional -> global.
comments: 2026-03-12 14:15 - Aisha Patel (Support): Notified customer and opened incident. Customer confirms they started a concurrency ramp as part of a load test at 14:00 PDT.
2026-03-12 14:27 - Marco Ramirez (SRE): Identified OOM restarts on runtime pods (exit code 137). Adding concurrency cap on tenant as emergency action.
2026-03-12 14:40 - LexiSearch (Customer): Confirmed temporary cap reduced failed sessions; requested ETA on permanent fix.

2026-03-12 15:05 - Jin Park (Runtime Eng): Reproduced local variant-swap memory spike. Agree that swaps can double peak RSS when triggered concurrently. Will add serialized swap and add soft memory guard. Referencing PR draft #8721.

2026-03-13 09:10 - Marco Ramirez (SRE): Gateway stream-limit applied at edge (max concurrent streams per connection=50) and route pinned. Monitoring shows stable metrics; closing customer-facing incident on our side pending eng patch. Keeping ticket open for follow-up and rollout.
